line	upstream/2026-09-20-lazy-panes-upstream-line-offers.md	Ten lines of kernel/kernel.py that exist byte-identically in upstream/main (a59c0cde3, fetched 2026-09-21; the branch heads the figure was measured at are named in the method's parenthetical below, and both heads are named wherever the figure is stated) were touched by fork PR 821 (the lazy panes): eight are modified at the head, and two were modified at one pass and restored byte-identical at a later one with a fork line inserted after each, so they stand unedited at the head and this offer carries them with their fork lines: the gear opener's `var sPend=false;` (restored in pass 6, the fork's `var sArmed=false,sOpen=null;` after it) and the reveal script's `var body={sid:sid,wid:wid(),via:via};if(boot)body.boot=true;` (joined with the fork's cols statement in pass 5, restored by that pass's verify fixer, the fork's `var cc=cols();if(cc>0)body.cols=cc;` after it); every pass label here is the author's build label, not a reviewer's round. THE SCOPE (the reviewer's round-6 ruling, extra6-1): this census is over kernel/kernel.py alone, the file where the fork's rule is to insert around upstream lines rather than modify them, so every figure in this entry (the ten, the eight modified and two restored, the fold cost of six, the four Python, five JavaScript and one markup line) counts lines of kernel/kernel.py; the branch's other changed files are outside this method and this disclosure, no figure is derived or quoted for them here, and the sibling entry 2026-09-18-lazy-panes-phone-skeleton-dial offers them whole (its where line names every changed path). THE METHOD (the reviewer's round-5 ruling): the population is derived by per-commit removal, never by the head's diff, since a line restored before the head leaves no trace there (the head-diff derivation this entry first stated found nine and could not see the reveal body line). Over every non-merge branch commit touching kernel/kernel.py since the merge base with origin/main, take the commit's removed lines against its parent, drop blank and brace-only lines, and test each byte-identical (the whole line, indentation included) against upstream/main's kernel.py; a line no branch commit ever removed is excluded (`userSwitch`, which the fork declares again after the project's line, is the control). The disambiguation against a coincidental duplicate is the same previous and next non-blank non-brace line in the parent and in upstream: nine of the ten match, the exception the f-files markup line, whose neighbours differ on both sides (a fork div before it; in upstream the `_data_pane_markup` splice after it), each of the ten occurring once in upstream. Re-run with git alone from a checkout with the fork as origin and the project as upstream (the script that also reads neighbours, provenance and language is outside the repo; this pipeline reproduces the population): `base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main); for c in $(git log --no-merges --format=%h $base..HEAD -- kernel/kernel.py); do git diff -U0 --output-indicator-old='~' "$c^" "$c" -- kernel/kernel.py | grep '^~' | cut -c2-; done | grep -vE '^[[:space:]{}()\[\];,]*$' | sort -u > removed.txt; git show upstream/main:kernel/kernel.py | grep -xF -f removed.txt | sort -u` (at 3ca8ecaef, the head the reviewer's round 5 ruled, 41 commits and 206 distinct removed lines; at 2828c25de, pass 7's last kernel.py commit and the parent of the pass-7 head 5feab4936, 46 and 245 (45 and 244 at 034c88ef9, an earlier pass-7 commit); at fc2648462, pass 8's last kernel.py commit (the author's label, 2026-09-21, taking the reviewer's round 6), 52 and 260: the six pass-8 kernel.py commits removed 15 distinct lines between them and none is byte-present in upstream/main; ten byte-present at each of the four heads against upstream/main a59c0cde3 (fetched 2026-09-21), the same ten by md5. The byte-present figure is a function of TWO heads, the branch's and upstream/main's, so every statement of it names both; every later kernel.py commit on the branch moves the first two figures and leaves the ten, so each figure here names the head it was measured at). The introducing commit, `git log upstream/main -S'<line>' --format='%h %an %ad' --date=short -- kernel/kernel.py | tail -1`, decides upstream-authored against fork-origin by its author field: a project maintainer's commit is upstream-authored, a fork commit the project took is fork-origin. The split of the ten kernel/kernel.py lines from that one derivation: eight upstream-authored, five by the project's commit of 2026-09-08 (`_reveal_request`'s signature, its `[reveal]` print, two lines, the /reveal route's call, and the reveal body line) and three by its commit of 2026-09-11 (`var sPend=false;` and the gear opener's load listener pair); two fork-origin lines the project took, the browse arm's `__rompMobileTab('feed')` (the browseFiles arm's copy of 2026-08-20, the date filed; the command's tail is the viewFile twin's commit of 2026-08-14, the line's first appearance, which the project removed on 2026-08-15, so three commits name the line and the tail is the twin's) and the f-files markup line (2026-09-10). By language, the ten lines of kernel/kernel.py: four Python lines (the signature, the print's two lines, the route's call), five JavaScript lines in the embedded scripts (four in `_LANDING_SETTINGS_JS`: the sPend declaration, the listener pair, the browse arm's tab swap; one in `_LANDING_REVEAL_JS`: the reveal body line), and one markup line in a Python string literal inside `def _landing()` (the f-files iframe). The fold cost, the upstream-authored lines of kernel/kernel.py modified at the head, is six lines of kernel/kernel.py: the listener pair, the signature, the print's two lines, the route's call; the two restored lines cost nothing, and the two fork-origin lines are outside it. The four Python lines' provenance is compound: `_reveal_request` was introduced by a fork commit of 2026-08-08 in a two-argument form and given its current shape by the project (2026-09-06, 2026-09-08), so the lines as they stand are the project's and the function the fork's. Each is a plain fix a maintainer would take: the reveal request carries the chat column count the shell posts so a parked reveal can name the one full for a one-column window; the gear opener arms its load listener once and opens at the LATEST tap's ask (before, every re-fetch after a dead document opened at the first tap's tab and section, and a listener per fetch was armed); the feed browse arm swaps tabs on the phone layout alone (on the desktop grid the swap persisted the remembered phone tab from a desktop gesture); the Files pane is served with data-src so it loads on its first show. Filed so the divergence is temporary: once offered and taken, the fold meets these lines as the project's own and the fork stops carrying them. Tier fix: each has a test that is red before it (the reveal body pins in `tests/test_kernel_webpush.py`, the two-line pin on the converted body line included, RelayArms in `tests/test_pane_state_broadcast.py`, the gated-switch pins in `tests/test_files_pane.py` and `tests/test_error_center.py`, the `f-files` pins in `tests/test_files_pane.py` and `tests/test_kernel_pane_rail.py`).
